declared_purpose: Control and inspect Tesla vehicles through teslapy, with local authentication caching, confirmation gates, and chat-friendly output (SKILL.md:1-29, 192-201). Supporting documentation adds per-vehicle odometer history in local SQLite for later analytics (README.md:175-181). Authentication, vehicle selection, requested readings, and command parameters support these purposes; broad payload reads, diagnostic history, and scheduler logs are implementation choices.

data_operations.operation: Read account identity and delegate authentication
data_operations.source: --email, TESLA_EMAIL, interactive email input, and manually pasted OAuth callback URL
data_operations.data_scope: Account email, authentication URL, callback URL containing OAuth material, and authorization state
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local CLI and teslapy.Tesla; intended Tesla authentication service through the dependency
data_operations.condition: When a handler calls get_tesla. The CLI prints the login URL and accepts the callback; it calls fetch_token when unauthorized. Browser interaction is performed by the user. Dependency-level transmissions are unresolved.

data_operations.data_scope: OAuth credentials and associated cache contents; exact schema is unavailable
data_operations.condition: Every get_tesla construction supplies this cache path. Existing cache files receive best-effort chmod 0600 after authentication handling. Local caching is an explicit requirement; actual dependency reads, writes, refreshes, and deletion are unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Read, persist, and display vehicle-selection defaults
data_operations.source: --car, MY_TESLA_DEFAULT_CAR, default-car input, and the local defaults file
data_operations.data_scope: Human-readable vehicle name or selection string and existing defaults
data_operations.condition: Explicit --car takes priority for selection; the environment default takes priority over the file. Setting default-car writes JSON and attempts chmod 0600. Showing the default requires no Tesla connection.

data_operations.operation: Enumerate account vehicles and select or display inventory
data_operations.data_scope: Returned vehicle inventory; handlers use display names, states, indices, default status, and mileage identifiers
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI memory; names and states go to caller stdout, while selection errors can list all vehicle names on stderr
data_operations.condition: Authentication, list, selected-vehicle handlers, and mileage recording enumerate vehicles. Normal auth/list output excludes VINs; list JSON uses an allowlist. Actual inventory transport and complete returned fields depend on teslapy.

data_operations.source: Vehicle state and, for mileage, the last successful recording timestamp
data_operations.data_scope: Selected vehicle association and wake request; mileage additionally computes elapsed recording age
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: teslapy.sync_wake_up(), intended Tesla API; progress and failures return to the caller
data_operations.condition: Ordinary reads permit waking unless --no-wake is set. Offline reads with --no-wake exit before vehicle-data retrieval. Mileage --no-wake always prevents waking; without that flag, waking is eligible when no successful point exists or the threshold, default 24 hours, has elapsed. Explicit wake directly invokes sync_wake_up.

data_operations.operation: Request vehicle data before selecting required fields
data_operations.data_scope: Full returned vehicle_data, potentially including precise drive_state coordinates and unrelated state sections
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: teslapy and the calling CLI process; subsequent handlers select fields locally
data_operations.condition: Status, summary, report, location, focused status commands, and online mileage recording use this call without a field selector. Returned data can remain with the caller; this is not evidence of onward disclosure. Whether narrower API retrieval is available is unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Return selected status fields and locally derived attributes
data_operations.source: Returned charge_state, climate_state, vehicle_state, and vehicle metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Requested vehicle status subsets, converted temperatures and pressures, formatted schedules, and openings summaries
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller stdout; helper results remain in the calling process
data_operations.condition: Summary/report defaults exclude location; focused handlers select relevant fields. The report's all_closed attribute is inferred from known openings: unknown fields are ignored, and at least one known field is required.

data_operations.operation: Return an explicitly selected raw payload
data_operations.data_scope: Entire payload, potentially including precise location and other fields omitted from sanitized output
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller stdout; persistence or forwarding requires caller behavior
data_operations.condition: The status handler outputs raw data when JSON is enabled; report and summary additionally require raw_json. These modes are documented. Global --json and --raw-json must precede the subcommand under the supplied parser; documented after-subcommand examples can fail parsing before handlers execute.

data_operations.operation: Read precise coordinates and produce location output
data_operations.data_scope: Precise coordinates in memory; rounded coordinates by default, or original coordinates with yes enabled
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller stdout, including a Google Maps URL containing the displayed coordinates
data_operations.condition: Only the location handler performs this output. Default rounding uses two decimal places; --digits accepts 0–6. Precise output uses the global --yes flag. Printing the Maps URL does not itself send coordinates to Google.

data_operations.source: Selected vehicle and user-supplied action parameters
data_operations.data_scope: Lock state requests, climate settings, charging settings, schedule time, trunk/window actions, seat and heater level, Sentry toggle, horn/light actions, and charge-port actions
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: teslapy.vehicle.command(), intended Tesla API and selected vehicle; confirmations return to caller stdout
data_operations.condition: Handlers send parameters needed for the selected action. Listed disruptive actions require yes, although gate placement varies. Window commands send fixed lat/lon placeholders rather than reading actual coordinates. Endpoint handling and remote persistence remain external unknowns.

data_operations.operation: Persist odometer samples and skipped-attempt records
data_operations.source: All account vehicles, current time, returned odometer, and prior successful records
data_operations.data_scope: Timestamp, id_s or vehicle_id, display name, odometer or null, state, source, and diagnostic note; skipped notes include wake policy and last-success time
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.my_tesla/mileage.sqlite or --db / MY_TESLA_MILEAGE_DB override; SQLite WAL mode is enabled
data_operations.condition: mileage record iterates all vehicles, independently of --car. Online vehicles produce odometer rows; skipped vehicles still produce null-odometer rows. init/status/export also initialize the database. No pruning is performed by the supplied mileage actions.

data_operations.operation: Read mileage history and return status or exports
data_operations.data_scope: Latest successful sample per vehicle for status; all stored fields and rows for export unless a time cutoff is supplied; JSON also includes the database path
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI memory and caller stdout; documented shell redirection creates caller-chosen CSV/JSON files
data_operations.condition: mileage status/export require no Tesla authentication. since_ts takes priority over since_days. Filtering limits exported rows, not stored history. Status fetches all successful rows before selecting the latest locally.

data_operations.operation: Optionally persist scheduler configuration and recurring output
data_operations.source: README launchd example and mileage record output
data_operations.data_scope: TESLA_EMAIL in scheduler configuration; JSON results containing vehicle identifiers, names, states, odometers, timestamps, database path, and recording/wake outcomes; stderr diagnostics
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.mytesla.mileage.plist and configured StandardOutPath / StandardErrorPath values ~/.my_tesla/mileage.log and ~/.my_tesla/mileage.err.log
data_operations.condition: Only if the user creates and loads the documented hourly job. The package does not install it automatically. Actual launchd expansion of the literal path values is not established by the supplied source.

data_operations.operation: Return error details and optional tracebacks
data_operations.source: Selection failures, wake failures, and caught exceptions
data_operations.data_scope: Vehicle names, selection input, vehicle state, exception text, code paths, and stack frames
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller stderr; additionally the scheduler error log if configured
data_operations.condition: Errors print exception text by default. --debug or MY_TESLA_DEBUG=1 adds a traceback. The source does not establish that dependency exception messages are sanitized or contain credentials.

data_operations.operation: Process synthetic test fixtures and clean development artifacts
data_operations.source: Packaged unit-test fixtures and repository bytecode files
data_operations.data_scope: Synthetic vehicle/default/mileage data, temporary environment overrides, in-memory or temporary databases, and Python bytecode
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Test-process memory and temporary directories; the test runner deletes repository __pycache__ directories and .pyc files
data_operations.condition: Only when tests or the helper are run. Representative command tests mock Tesla access; temporary-directory contexts clean fixture files. Bytecode cleanup is unrelated to deleting production tokens, defaults, mileage history, or logs.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated vehicle_data sections, including precise location when returned for non-location status or odometer requests
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: teslapy and CLI memory at the get_vehicle_data return boundary
potential_excess.condition: Sanitized/focused readings and mileage recording request the full payload before selecting fields.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The required outcome is the requested status subset or odometer sample. Sanitized output explicitly excludes location; full-payload collection is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain the fields needed for the requested view or recording, while retaining explicitly requested raw and location capabilities.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use narrower endpoint or field selection if supported. Otherwise discard unrelated sections immediately and document that acquisition cannot be narrowed with the available API.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Selective retrieval support is blocking and unverified because teslapy is absent. Local filtering alone cannot reduce data already returned to the process. Preserve full responses for explicit raw-output requests.

potential_excess.data_scope: All account vehicles and their display names and states during authentication
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Additional vehicle_list dependency call, CLI memory, and caller stdout
potential_excess.condition: cmd_auth enumerates and prints vehicles after establishing authentication.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Authentication requires authorization and local credential caching. Vehicle enumeration is separately provided by list and is not an explicit authentication requirement.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Authenticate and confirm the local cache outcome.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the authentication-time inventory action or make it an explicit option; retain list for requested enumeration.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep authentication success and cache-location reporting. This removes a redundant action rather than fields from a required inventory response.

potential_excess.data_scope: Timestamped identifiers, names, states, wake-policy details, and last-success information for attempts with no odometer measurement
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: mileage_points in the local SQLite database/WAL, subsequently included in exports
potential_excess.condition: Every skipped sleeping/offline vehicle receives a null-odometer row.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared tracking purpose is odometer history. Historical failed-attempt records are an additional diagnostic persistence choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Skip unavailable cars, report the current skip, and retain successful measurements for history and wake eligibility.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Avoid inserting skipped rows, or retain only a short-lived latest diagnostic record per vehicle.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep caller-visible skip results. The wake-age query already ignores null odometers, so removing skipped history preserves its successful-capture calculation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated vehicle display names and raw API identifiers, plus per-sample state/source metadata beyond timestamp and odometer
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Successful mileage rows in SQLite/WAL and default CSV/JSON exports
potential_excess.condition: Every successful recording repeats these fields; exports include them by default.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Per-vehicle odometer analytics and last-success tracking need stable linkage, timestamps, and measurements. Repeated names and diagnostic metadata are implementation choices.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Maintain reliable per-vehicle history and readable identification.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Keep a single vehicle mapping and use a local key in sample rows. Make diagnostic state/source fields optional in routine storage and exports.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve vehicle distinction, latest readable names, odometer history, and wake-threshold queries. Offer explicit detailed exports where consumers require the existing metadata.

potential_excess.data_scope: A second recurring history of vehicle identifiers, names, odometers, states, timestamps, and local database path
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The optional launchd job's configured StandardOutPath, ~/.my_tesla/mileage.log
potential_excess.condition: The documented hourly job requests JSON output and redirects stdout to a log in addition to recording SQLite rows.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Mileage history is already persisted in SQLite. A second detailed history in scheduler logs is not required for that outcome.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Record measurements and provide enough operational feedback to detect failures.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Discard routine scheduler stdout or add counts-only output; retain bounded, sanitized diagnostics.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep database recording, manual status/export commands, and useful failure reporting. Normal interactive JSON returns need not be removed.

potential_excess.data_scope: Authentication/cache handling, account vehicle enumeration, and potentially a wake request for an action ultimately refused
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local credential cache and CLI; teslapy's intended Tesla authentication, enumeration, and wake boundaries
potential_excess.condition: Charge, scheduled-charging, and Sentry mutations ensure online status before checking yes. Windows, seats, and charge-port mutations authenticate and select a vehicle before checking yes.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The explicit safety requirement is to refuse these mutations without confirmation. Preparing a refused operation does not require account inventory or waking.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Reject an unconfirmed mutation and explain the required flag.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Check confirmation for mutating actions before constructing the Tesla client, enumerating vehicles, or attempting wake-up.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain read-only status paths without confirmation and preserve confirmed command behavior. Already-online vehicles may avoid an actual wake request; dependency authentication activity is conditional.

potential_excess.data_scope: Wake requests associated with account vehicles during default mileage recording
potential_excess.condition: mileage record omits --no-wake and a sleeping vehicle has no successful sample or exceeds the default 24-hour threshold.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: README explicitly declares no-wake behavior by default. The parser defaults no_wake to false, making threshold-based waking eligible without a separate opt-in.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Record online cars and skip sleeping cars under the documented default policy.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Default mileage recording to no wake and require explicit opt-in for threshold-based waking.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue recording all online vehicles and retain an explicit threshold-wake mode. The supplied --no-wake examples currently prohibit waking even after the threshold.

unknowns: Blocking external verification: teslapy source is not supplied. Actual endpoints, request/response fields, caching versus network retrieval, telemetry, token refresh/revocation, and remote retention cannot be established. Packaged call-site review is complete.
Whether Tesla/teslapy supports narrower vehicle-data retrieval is unresolved; eliminating unrelated inbound fields is therefore conditional.

Caller, agent, chat, terminal, and external log retention or forwarding are unspecified. Stdout/stderr returns alone do not establish third-party disclosure. Google receives no demonstrated request merely because a Maps URL is printed.
Actual cache/default permission enforcement is best-effort. Mileage database/WAL and scheduler-log permissions depend on the environment; no explicit restrictive permission setting is shown for them.

No packaged retention period or user-data deletion command is specified for authentication caches, defaults, mileage history, or scheduler logs. External cleanup and dependency-managed deletion are unknown.

The scope and historical detail needed for future mileage analytics are unspecified. Proposed metadata reductions preserve basic per-vehicle odometer history, but additional analytics requirements could justify selected fields.

Dependency exception contents are unknown, so credential or location exposure through errors cannot be confirmed. The optional launchd example's literal tilde-containing log paths also have unresolved runtime resolution.
